$comment: One note per engine behaviour, keyed by ref to the id in packages/engine's registry. The rules panel shows the engine's own id, label and cite; this file adds the sentence a player reads. scripts/labels-check.test.ts fails when a behaviour has no note or a note has no behaviour. `title` is the plain sentence the panel lists a behaviour under; the engine id shows only once the row is opened.
title: Rules panel notes
label: invention

records.text: One six-sided die. The book has no other.
records.title: The die is a d6, and only a d6

records.text: Two dice read as a two-digit address, first die tens, second die ones: the Technique, Ritual and word tables.
records.title: Two dice make a two-digit address on the big tables

records.text: Two dice summed, with both faces kept so a doubles result can be shown and a save replayed.
records.title: Two dice are summed, and doubles are noticed

records.text: SKILL is 1d6+6, ENDURANCE 2d6+12, LUCK 1d6+6.
records.title: SKILL, ENDURANCE and LUCK are rolled, not chosen

records.text: The rolled values are kept as the Master's initial values beside the current ones; later rules refer back to them.
records.title: Your starting numbers are remembered beside your current ones

records.text: One d6 for social status, and the gold that comes with it.
records.title: One die decides your station in life and your gold

records.text: Common clothing, one weapon, and a Health Elixir or a Market item under 20 GP.
records.title: You begin with clothes, a weapon and one small thing

records.text: The free-text starting weapon counts as a weapon for any armed Proficiency.
records.title: Whatever you wrote down as your weapon counts as one
records.says: a weapon, even if not listed in the weapon table
records.silent: which weapons count for which style
records.reversed: armed Proficiencies would add nothing until a Market weapon is bought

records.text: A Martial Art is chosen, or rolled on the banded d6 x d6 table of eighteen.
records.title: Your Martial Art is chosen, or rolled on the table of eighteen

records.text: The points to spend on Proficiencies equal the rolled SKILL, before any Training is deducted from it.
records.title: You have as many Proficiency points as your rolled SKILL

records.text: No Proficiency may exceed 4 at creation.
records.title: No Proficiency starts above 4

records.text: Proficiency points may be left unspent, and a Proficiency may be left at zero.
records.title: Points may be left unspent
records.says: spend as many points as your SKILL value
records.silent: whether every point must be spent
records.reversed: creation would flag every sheet with points left over

records.text: Each Training point bought at creation permanently lowers SKILL by one.
records.title: Each Training point costs one SKILL for good

records.text: Each Training point gives four Resource points; a Technique or Ritual costs its printed value in them.
records.title: Each Training point buys four points of Techniques and Rituals

records.text: Training is carried as a Proficiency with a value, usable in checks.
records.title: Training is a Proficiency you can roll on

records.text: Overspending a pool raises a flag with the numbers; the engine never refuses a creation.
records.title: Overspending is flagged, never refused

records.text: The author's eight sheets load exactly as printed, flags and all; nothing is corrected.
records.title: The eight printed Masters load exactly as printed

records.text: 2d6 against SKILL plus one relevant Proficiency; equal or under passes.
records.title: A SKILL check: 2d6 at or under SKILL plus one Proficiency

records.text: 2d6 against LUCK; equal or under passes.
records.title: A LUCK check: 2d6 at or under LUCK

records.text: Every LUCK check costs one LUCK, pass or fail.
records.title: Every LUCK check spends one LUCK, win or lose

records.text: Two sixes fail a check whatever the threshold. Sealed in spec.md; reopening it is a re-seed.
records.title: A double six always fails a check

records.text: Whether an action is a SKILL check or a LUCK check is the player's call; the engine offers both and picks neither.
records.title: You decide whether an action is SKILL or LUCK

records.text: Each side's Attack Strength is 2d6 plus SKILL plus one relevant Proficiency.
records.title: Attack Strength is 2d6 plus SKILL plus one Proficiency

records.text: Exactly one Proficiency enters a roll, never two.
records.title: Only one Proficiency counts in a roll

records.text: Training's value adds to checks made to perform or resist Techniques, not to Attack Strength.
records.title: Training does not add to Attack Strength
records.says: use Training skill as one of your Martial Proficiency
records.silent: which rolls it applies to
records.reversed: every trained Master would roll higher in every round

records.text: Where a stat block lists two Proficiencies, the engine adds the higher unless the narrative or a Special result names the other.
records.title: An opponent with two Proficiencies uses the higher
records.says: one relevant Martial Proficiency (if any)
records.silent: which of two, for a foe carrying both
records.reversed: every two-Proficiency foe would hit for less

records.text: When the opponent's total is higher, the Master loses the difference from ENDURANCE.
records.title: When they roll higher, you lose the difference

records.text: When the Master's total is higher, choose one: strike for the difference, use a Technique, change or recover a weapon, or create an Opening.
records.title: When you roll higher, you choose one of four things

records.text: In combat a Technique is available only as the winner's option in a round; outside combat, at any time.
records.title: In a fight, a Technique is the winner's choice for the round
records.says: use one of the Techniques you know
records.silent: whether a Technique may be used when behind
records.reversed: changes every fight already played

records.text: A Technique used in combat needs no roll and costs its value in ENDURANCE.
records.title: A Technique needs no roll and costs its value in ENDURANCE

records.text: Creating an Opening does no damage; it makes a Final Blow possible.
records.title: An Opening does no damage but sets up the Final Blow

records.text: A fight ends when a Final Blow lands, either side's ENDURANCE reaches zero, or an Unexpected Event occurs.
records.title: A fight ends on a Final Blow, an ENDURANCE of zero, or an Unexpected Event

records.text: After an Opening, roll 2d6; doubles land the blow, six chances in thirty-six.
records.title: The Final Blow lands on doubles

records.text: A double six lands a doubles roll; the fumble rule is for checks only. Sealed in spec.md.
records.title: A double six lands a Final Blow

records.text: A landed Final Blow may become a new Technique: roll against LUCK, then give it a value of 1-4 and a description.
records.title: A landed Final Blow can become a Technique of your own

records.text: The Final Blow's LUCK roll costs one LUCK on a failure only; a success costs nothing.
records.title: Failing to keep a new Technique costs one LUCK; succeeding costs nothing
records.says: on a failure, lose 1 LUCK
records.silent: whether the ordinary LUCK-check decrement also applies
records.reversed: every kept Technique would cost a point of LUCK

records.text: A Praying Mantis Master's landed Final Blow kills; the doubles roll itself is unchanged.
records.title: A Praying Mantis Master's Final Blow kills
records.says: finishing blow is always lethal
records.silent: whether the style changes the roll or only the outcome
records.reversed: the Mantis would land blows more often instead of harder

records.text: The Final Blow table gives three words for inspiration; composing the name is the player's.
records.title: The naming table is inspiration; the name is yours

records.text: Equal Attack Strengths are an Unexpected Event.
records.title: A tie is an Unexpected Event

records.text: After an Unexpected Event you are no longer in the combat phase; the 2d6 table is rolled only if the narrative leaves the event unclear.
records.title: After an Unexpected Event, the fight is over

records.text: Nine of the eleven rows state no mechanical effect; the engine carries a minimum reading for each and labels it so.
records.title: Each Unexpected Event row has a smallest reading, and it is labelled
records.says: the row's text, and nothing else, for rows 2-5 and 9-12
records.silent: what an injury, a lost weapon or a divine intervention does to the numbers
records.reversed: those rows would be narration with no effect on the sheet

records.text: Row 7's 1-4 Minions are read off a d6: 1-2 one, 3 two, 4 three, 5-6 four.
records.title: How many Minions arrive is read off a d6
records.says: 1-4 Minions of the same type
records.silent: how to roll 1-4 in a d6-only game
records.reversed: a different spread of reinforcements

records.text: The two Enemy-retreat rows roll Morale on a d6: 1-3 it flees, 4-5 a cautious retreat, 6 it rallies with 1d6 more. Ours, sealed in spec.md.
records.title: When the enemy would retreat, Morale decides whether they can

records.text: Against several opponents the Master's SKILL is reduced by their number.
records.title: Against several foes, your SKILL drops by their number

records.text: An opponent's ATTACK is how many of its kind may attack at once.
records.title: ATTACK is how many of a kind can strike at once

records.text: ATTACK counts opponents a creature can wound at once and does nothing against a lone Master. Sealed in spec.md.
records.title: ATTACK does nothing against a Master fighting alone

records.text: The one stat block printed with a blank ATTACK is read as 1.
records.title: A blank ATTACK is read as 1
records.says: nothing; the cell is blank
records.silent: the number
records.reversed: a stronger Huang Feng Guai

records.text: In multiple combat the Master rolls once a round and that roll is compared against each attacker's own roll.
records.title: You roll once a round and it faces every attacker
records.says: reduce your SKILL by the number of opponents
records.silent: how many rolls are made
records.reversed: one roll per opponent, and a very different fight

records.text: An area Technique deals the same damage to each opponent it reaches, not a share of it.
records.title: An area Technique hurts each foe it reaches the same

records.text: How many opponents an area Technique reaches is read from its printed text: two, or all around.
records.title: How far an area Technique reaches is what its text says
records.says: Butterfly Palms, Light Body, Exploding Qi, Double Strike
records.silent: a number for each
records.reversed: every area Technique would reach the same count

records.text: Fleeing without a stratagem costs a last blow of 2 ENDURANCE.
records.title: Fleeing without a trick costs a last blow of 2

records.text: Each escape that costs damage scores one Dishonor Point.
records.title: An escape that cost blood scores a Dishonor Point

records.text: A stratagem is any escape Technique or a player-declared one the Oracle approves; the last blow is damage, so a bare escape always scores Dishonor.
records.title: A trick spares the last blow, and the last blow is damage
records.says: a Technique or some other stratagem
records.silent: what counts, and whether the last blow is damage
records.reversed: a bare escape would cost ENDURANCE but no Dishonor

records.text: SKILL recovers one point from a regeneration Technique and fully after a night's rest.
records.title: SKILL comes back fully after a night's rest

records.text: ENDURANCE recovers four from a healing Technique, a meal or an Elixir, and fully after a week's rest.
records.title: ENDURANCE comes back 4 at a time, fully after a week

records.text: LUCK recovers one point from a Spirituality check at a Temple, with incense.
records.title: LUCK comes back one point at a time, at a temple

records.text: The book gives LUCK no full restore, so the engine invents none.
records.title: LUCK never comes back all at once

records.text: A night's rest heals 4 ENDURANCE. Ours, sealed in spec.md.
records.title: A night's rest heals 4 ENDURANCE

records.text: At an adventure's end, four scores of 1-3 are summed and Dishonor subtracted: that is the XP.
records.title: XP is four scores of 1 to 3, less Dishonor

records.text: What an advance costs depends on the Master's SKILL band.
records.title: What an advance costs depends on your SKILL

records.text: The band is read from current SKILL at the moment of spending.
records.title: The cost is read from your SKILL at the moment you spend
records.says: the worked example uses the current value
records.silent: current or initial SKILL
records.reversed: a Master whose SKILL fell would pay a different price

records.text: SKILL and LUCK cannot exceed 12.
records.title: SKILL and LUCK stop at 12

records.text: After creation a Proficiency may rise past 4.
records.title: After creation a Proficiency can pass 4

records.text: Unspent XP waits for the next advancement.
records.title: Unspent XP waits for next time

records.text: The four scores are the player's own; the engine flags an odd total and refuses nothing.
records.title: The four scores are yours to give; nothing is refused

records.text: A defeated opponent's treasure is 1d6 on the band its ENDURANCE falls in.
records.title: A beaten foe's treasure depends on how tough it was

records.text: The treasure roll is always offered after a victory and may be declined.
records.title: The treasure roll is offered after every victory, and you may decline it
records.says: if you believe that your defeated opponents may be in possession of something
records.silent: when the belief applies
records.reversed: the app would have to guess when a foe carries anything

records.text: A spirit or ghost is immune to ordinary blows; a Technique, Ritual or exceptional weapon is needed.
records.title: Spirits and ghosts shrug off ordinary blows

records.text: An opponent's Martial Arts (n) gives every Proficiency n points; its Techniques add their value with no ENDURANCE cost.
records.title: An opponent's Martial Arts value counts for every Proficiency

records.text: The Oracle's Special enemy attack uses one of the opponent's listed Proficiencies this round.
records.title: A Special enemy attack uses one of its listed Proficiencies
records.says: Special, and nothing more
records.silent: what a Special attack does
records.reversed: Special would be narration only

records.text: An Oracle Ambush is one unopposed opening round for the opponent.
records.title: An Ambush gives the enemy one free round
records.says: Ambush and Attack as two outcomes
records.silent: what separates them mechanically
records.reversed: Ambush and Attack would play identically

records.text: The book throws dice on a sheet of paper; the app places each point from dice so a saved region lands the same way twice.
records.title: The region is dice thrown on a sheet of paper
records.says: roll a handful of d6 on a sheet of paper; mark where the dice land
records.silent: how an app without paper does that
records.reversed: a region could not be replayed from its record

records.text: Each point's Location is the face its die shows, read on the Region table.
records.title: Each place is the face its die shows

records.text: Points are linked to their nearest neighbours. Ours.
records.title: Places are linked to their nearest neighbours

records.text: Where nearest-neighbour links leave islands, the closest pair across the gap is joined so the region can be walked. Ours; joined links are marked.
records.title: No part of the region is cut off

records.text: A link's miles are the sum of the two dice that measured it; the book calls the scale arbitrary. Ours.
records.title: A road's miles are the two dice that measured it

records.text: The same 2d6 reads the route type on the book's table: nothing, mule track, trail, beaten path, paved road.
records.title: The same dice say what kind of road it is

records.text: Where a point sits on the screen means nothing; the diagram says it is not to scale. Ours.
records.title: The map is not to scale

records.text: An adventure declares the format version its files are written in. The engine reads version 1 and refuses anything else rather than guessing at an unfamiliar shape.
records.title: An adventure written for a newer build is refused, not guessed at
Standing where an adventure starts is not the same as having entered it
records.text: A Master who has just been made stands at the adventure's start area but has not visited it. The visit is recorded when they actually walk in - out of Fen Pass and up the trail - which is what lets the app tell an adventure that has not begun from one that has. The book draws no such line; this one is ours.
Every time you enter an area, roll 1d6 on the adventure's event table: Ambush, Encounter, Safe exploration or Hint.
records.title: Entering an area rolls the Event table

records.text: On an Ambush or an Encounter, roll for the creature encountered in this area on the area's own table.
records.title: An Ambush or an Encounter rolls for who is here

records.text: You may walk from an area only into the areas its file lists as exits.
records.title: You can only walk where the map draws a way
records.says: the adventure prints a cave map with passages drawn between chambers, and no list of exits
records.silent: which chamber connects to which, and which chamber the entrance arrow points into
records.source: estate-inventory.md, I-42, section 4.4 - read off a 4x render of the printed plan
records.reversed: any area could be entered from any other, and the locked Private Quarters would stop gating anything

records.text: The Chieftain quarter and the Women quarter are both locked, and the private quarter's key opens both. Either attendant carries a copy.
records.title: One key opens both private quarters
records.says: the Attendants room is entrance to the locked Private Quarters, and both attendants carry private quarter's key
records.silent: which rooms the Private Quarters are, and whether one key opens both
records.source: estate-inventory.md, I-07, with the map's layout
records.reversed: two keys would be needed and an attendant met alone could leave the quarters unopenable

records.text: An area whose encounter line prints no dice always meets the same foes, on any Ambush or Encounter.
records.title: An area with no dice on its line always meets the same foes
records.says: the Storage room and the Kitchen print Devil servants, and the Women quarter prints Old Vixen and she-Devil servant, with no dice beside them
records.silent: what to roll in an area whose encounter line has no dice
records.source: estate-inventory.md, I-34; the number of devils comes from the Oracle's No. of enemies row
records.reversed: those three areas would have no defined encounter and the event roll would do nothing there

records.text: A named foe defeated once is gone from every table they appear in. The Junior King met on the mountain is the same Junior King as in the Dining Hall.
records.title: A named foe beaten once is gone for good
records.says: the event roll is made every time you enter an area, re-entry included, and the Kings appear in several areas' encounter lines
records.silent: whether a defeated opponent comes back when the area is entered again
records.source: estate-inventory.md, I-33b and I-33c; rank and file - servants, Ogres, Woodgatherers - stay unlimited
records.reversed: the Senior King could be killed for his fan once per visit, and the cave would never empty

records.text: An encounter row that meets nothing turns the event into a safe exploration instead.
records.title: Meeting nothing is a safe exploration
records.says: the Chieftain quarter's encounter line reads 5-6 Empty
records.silent: what an Ambush that meets Empty does
records.reversed: an Ambush in the Chieftain quarter would have to resolve against no opponent at all

records.text: While a flag holds, a foe is not met in an area. Opening the gourd makes it night, and the Cave entrance's Ogres are out hunting.
records.title: Some foes are away while something holds, like night
records.says: the gourd swallows the sky, changing day to night, and the Ogres go out hunting for travellers once a day
records.silent: what night does mechanically
records.source: estate-inventory.md, I-45, with the day-and-night flag of I-40
records.reversed: night would be scenery, and the gourd would have no use inside the cave

records.text: An area's hint and a treasure's workings stay hidden until earned: a Hint event, information about the area, holding the treasure, or reading the Chieftain's sheets.
records.title: Hints and the treasures' workings stay hidden until earned
records.says: read this part only if your PG gets information about the area or with Event roll=Hint, and read this if you want to know the treasure's way of working
records.silent: how a reader who is also the player is meant to un-read a paragraph
records.source: estate-inventory.md, I-60, with I-06b on what counts as information
records.reversed: every hint and every treasure effect would be on screen from the first turn, and the adventure would have no secrets

records.text: The gourd on the Storage room's shelves and the vase on the Attendants room's pedestal are picked up by exploring, not taken off a body.
records.title: Some treasures are found lying there, not carried by a foe
records.says: a jade vase is guarded on a pedestal, and one of the treasures looks like an ordinary gourd bottle
records.silent: which encounter drops those two treasures - no stat block lists either
records.reversed: two of the five treasures would be unobtainable, and the adventure could not be finished

records.text: The Monk tied up in the Kitchen pool is a rescue, not an enemy. Free him for his loot; attack him and score a Dishonor Point.
records.title: Attacking a captive costs a Dishonor Point
records.says: the man is a MONK, captured to be eaten, and he is printed with SKILL, ENDURANCE, ATTACK, special skills and loot like any opponent
records.silent: whether the Monk is an enemy, and what killing him costs
records.reversed: the Monk would be one more encounter and the Kitchen would hold no rescue at all

records.text: An adventure marks its progress with acts, tested in order; the highest one you satisfy is where you are, and the last one is the ending screen.
records.title: The adventure climbs through acts, and the last is the ending

records.text: One record holds a whole campaign: the Master, the deeds ledger, what you wrote, how many rolls you typed, and each adventure's own memory of what you did there.
records.title: One record holds the whole campaign

records.text: When the Master dies the record can be read but not continued. Starting again starts a new world; the old one is not inherited.
records.title: When the Master dies, the world dies too

records.text: A Master created over a creation pool is created anyway and carries an overspend mark for the rest of the campaign.
records.title: An overspent Master is created anyway and marked

records.text: Typing the faces of a roll instead of rolling them adds one to the record's override count. The count is never reset.
records.title: Typing a roll instead of rolling it is counted

records.text: There is no account and no cloud. The exported JSON file is the backup, and it opens on any build that can still read its version.
records.title: The exported file is the only backup

records.text: An old save is brought forward by a chain of migrations, each named for the estate reading whose position changed and forced it.
records.title: An old save is carried forward, one reading at a time

records.text: A file that cannot be opened comes back with a reason - not JSON, not a campaign, or from a newer build - rather than an error.
records.title: A file that cannot be read says why

records.text: The trail-head village is the same three locations on every run. The book describes a City; this settlement is ours.
records.title: The village is the same every time

records.text: One path leaves the village, and it climbs to the Flat-top mountain and the Lotus Flower cave.
records.title: One trail leaves the village, and it climbs to the cave

records.text: One gold piece is ten silver. Prices are compared in silver so a purse never holds half a coin.
records.title: A gold piece is ten silver

records.text: Goods at the stall row cost what the Market table prints. Nobody haggles with someone walking toward the mountain.
records.title: Goods cost what the book prints

records.text: A purchase you cannot afford leaves your purse exactly as it was.
records.title: What you cannot afford costs nothing

records.text: Without incense there is no attempt at the shrine, and no dice are rolled.
records.title: No incense, no prayer

records.text: A successful Spirituality check at the three stars recovers 1 LUCK - the only way LUCK comes back.
records.title: A prayer that is heard recovers 1 LUCK

records.text: One Spirituality check at the shrine per day. A second is not rolled.
records.title: The gods listen once a day
records.says: a Spirituality check recovers 1 LUCK, with no count on how often
records.silent: how many times a day the gods will listen
records.reversed: LUCK could be refilled to full in one afternoon at one shrine

records.text: The inn takes the room price first. If you cannot pay it, nothing else happens either.
records.title: The inn is paid before it feeds you

records.text: The meal and the night are the same +4 ENDURANCE, applied once, not two bonuses that stack.
records.title: The meal and the bed are one recovery, not two

records.text: A full night's rest restores SKILL completely and ENDURANCE by 4.
records.title: A night at the inn restores SKILL and 4 ENDURANCE
